ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the altitude to side $BC$, $AE$ and $BF$ are the angle bisectors of $\angle BAC$ and $\angle ABC$ respectively, $\angle BAC=56^\circ$, $\angle C=70^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle BOA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: In $\triangle ABC$, we have $\angle ABC=180^\circ-\angle C-\angle BAC=180^\circ-70^\circ-56^\circ=54^\circ$ \\
Since $BF$ bisects $\angle ABC$ \\
Therefore, $\angle 1=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC=\frac{1}{2}\times 54^\circ=27^\circ$ \\
Therefore, $AE$ bisects $\angle BAC$ \\
Therefore, $\angle 2=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAC=\frac{1}{2}\times 56^\circ=28^\circ$ \\
Therefore, in $\triangle AOB$, $\angle AOB=180^\circ-(\angle 1+\angle 2)=180^\circ-(27^\circ+28^\circ)=\boxed{125^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; AD is perpendicular from A to BC, and there is a right-angle mark at D; from A to E on BC a line segment AE is drawn; from B to F on AC a line segment BF is drawn; AE and BF intersect at point O inside the triangle, so O is at the intersection point of the two angle bisectors AE and BF. Reasoning: The problem gives that AE bisects ∠BAC, and BF bisects ∠ABC, so O is the incenter of triangle ABC. For incenter O, the angle formed by the two internal angle bisectors OA and OB satisfies the incenter angle theorem: ∠AOB = 90° + 1/2∠C. It is known that ∠C = 70°, so ∠BOA = ∠AOB = 90° + 35° = 125°.
